backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/organizations/members.rs — the three org-membership mutation handlers (add_organization_member :206, update_organization_member :429, and the delete handler at :717) gate on a single coarse permission flag (users:create / users:update / users:delete) plus a role-belongs-to-org check. They are otherwise correctly tenant-scoped. But two standard org-RBAC guardrails are ABSENT.

(1) No privilege-ceiling / anti-escalation check: update_organization_member (:509-539) validates only that req.role_id exists and belongs to the org — it never compares the target role's privilege set against the acting admin's own. Any member holding users:update can therefore assign ANY role in the org (including owner) to another member OR to themselves (no target_user_id != admin_user_id self-guard on the update path).

(2) No last-owner protection: neither update_organization_member nor the delete handler checks the remaining owner/admin count before demoting (:576-585) or removing (:717+) a member. Nothing prevents the sole remaining owner from being demoted/removed, orphaning the organization.

Impact: authorization completeness / defense-in-depth. Both are model-dependent (severity hinges on whether users:update is grantable to non-owner roles). Backend-only fix (+ possibly a role_repo helper for privilege comparison and an owner-count query). Cloud-build-blocked at implementer time by api-server swagger-ui egress #2949 until #2949 lands.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/multi_currency.rs:373-411 — the exchange-rate-refresh handler is a STUB that reports success. Comment: `// For now, we just log the attempt`. It logs `log_rate_fetch(..., success=true, count=0)` and returns HTTP 200 `{"success": true, "message": "Exchange rate fetch initiated"}`. Callers cannot distinguish 'rates refreshed' from 'no-op stub'; downstream conversions keep using stale rates while the API reports success.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/multi_currency.rs:406 — `let _ = s.multi_currency_repo.update_last_rate_update(org_id).await;` swallows the timestamp-write error; the success arm still returns success=true even if this UPDATE failed. Contrast sibling writes in the same handler which correctly map_err to 500.

Impact: LOW — correctness/observability smell on an org-scoped admin action. Fix: either wire real ECB/XE fetch or make the stub's response honest (501 / stub:true flag); replace let _ = at :406 with map_err(...) or tracing::warn!. Cloud-build-blocked at implementer time by #2949 until it lands.

ppt-web documents feature ships hardcoded Slovak user-facing error/empty/loading strings that bypass react-i18next (t()), so users on the app's other supported locales (cs/de/en) see Slovak text on these states. Occurrences: MoveFolderDialog.tsx:429/:434; DocumentsPage.tsx:429/:438 (tier1d cited DocumentsBrowse.tsx — actual file is DocumentsPage.tsx); FolderTree.tsx:608/:618; DocumentDetail.tsx:145; FolderTreePage.tsx:75; DocumentPreviewModal.tsx:56; PdfPreview.tsx:269 (missing diacritics in 'nacitani' confirms hand-written literals, not catalog entries).

Inconsistent with the same files' own norm: MoveFolderDialog.tsx already uses t() for aria labels; DocumentsPage.tsx wraps other copy in t(). Landable frontend-only remedy: move each string into the i18n catalog and wrap in t() (add useTranslation where a file lacks it).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/meters/components/ReadingForm.tsx:107-116 — in handlePhotoChange, OCR failure is caught with only `console.error('OCR processing failed')` and no user-facing signal. Comment 'OCR failed, user can still enter value manually' documents graceful degradation, but users see no toast/banner/inline note and may wait expecting the value field to auto-fill.

console.error also logs a bare message without the caught error object. Landable frontend-only remedy: surface a non-blocking inline hint/toast on OCR failure (via i18n catalog) and include the error in the console.error call. Low severity: no data loss, manual entry still works.
